skill.name: dcg
skill.description: Destructive Command Guard is a Claude Code safety hook that reviews Bash commands before execution and blocks known destructive patterns.
skill.summary: Block destructive shell commands before Claude Code runs them.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by documentation of commands that DCG is designed to block. The real risks are the quick-install curl-to-bash patterns, the sudo installer path, persistent Claude Code hook configuration, and the documented bypass variable.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash and sudo bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with download, checksum verification, script review, and then explicit execution steps. Avoid sudo installation unless required.

remediation.issue: The guard can be bypassed with DCG_BYPASS=1.
remediation.suggestion: Document when bypass is acceptable, log or alert on bypass use, and discourage it in shared or CI-like agent environments.

remediation.issue: The hook requires persistent changes to hidden Claude Code settings.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to back up ~/.claude/settings.json and review the exact hook entry before applying it.

content.value_statement: AI coding agents can accidentally run commands that delete work or damage infrastructure. This skill adds a fast guardrail for Claude Code Bash hooks that blocks known destructive patterns before execution.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install a Rust command guard for Claude Code Bash hooks.
Documents blocked command patterns for git, filesystems, databases, containers, Kubernetes, cloud tools, and infrastructure tools.
Shows Claude Code PreToolUse hook configuration for running the guard before Bash commands.
Provides examples of allowed safe patterns such as dry runs and force-with-lease pushes.
Describes configuration through packs, environment variables, and a TOML config file.
limitations: It does not inspect commands inside external scripts.
It only covers known destructive patterns and allows unknown commands by default.
It is designed for well-intentioned agent mistakes, not malicious users.
Installation instructions include remote shell execution that users must review before running.

use_cases.title: Protect active development work
use_cases.description: Block accidental git resets, forced checkouts, and recursive deletion commands during agent-assisted coding sessions.

use_cases.title: Add guardrails for agent teams
use_cases.description: Standardize command safety checks across Claude Code sessions that run frequent Bash operations.

use_cases.title: Audit risky shell command patterns
use_cases.description: Review documented patterns for destructive database, container, cloud, and infrastructure commands before enabling packs.

prompt_templates.title: Install the guard safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review the DCG installation steps before I run them. Explain what each command changes and which steps need extra caution.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Claude Code hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect DCG to Claude Code with a PreToolUse Bash hook, and explain how I can test that it blocks git reset --hard.

prompt_templates.title: Choose safety packs
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a DCG pack configuration for a team that uses Git, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and PostgreSQL. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate command coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our risky shell command workflows and map them to DCG packs. Identify commands that DCG will not inspect and suggest compensating controls.

output_examples.input: Test whether git reset --hard should run through Claude Code.
output_examples.output: The guard blocks the command and explains that it destroys uncommitted changes. It suggests saving work first before running the command manually.

output_examples.input: Configure only Docker and Kubernetes protections.
output: Enable the kubernetes pack or selected sub-packs.
Restart Claude Code after updating the hook configuration.

output_examples.input: Check whether rm -rf in a temp directory is allowed.
output_examples.output: The documented policy allows recursive deletion inside temporary directories, but blocks similar commands against home or project paths.

best_practices: Review remote installation scripts before piping them to a shell.
Start with core protections, then enable extra packs that match tools your team uses.
Test hook behavior with harmless sample commands before relying on it in real projects.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the guard as protection against malicious users or compromised scripts.
Do not enable bypass variables in shared agent environments.
Do not run the sudo installation path unless system-wide installation is required and reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands by itself?
faq.answer: The skill documentation does not execute commands, but it provides installation and test commands for users to run.

faq.question: Why is the audit strict about the installer?
faq.answer: The quick install pipes remote content into a shell. That is convenient but risky unless the script is reviewed first.

faq.question: Can DCG stop every destructive command?
faq.answer: No. It blocks known Bash patterns and allows unknown commands by default.

faq.question: Does it protect non-Bash tools?
faq.answer: No. The documented hook targets Claude Code Bash tool calls.

faq.question: Can users override a block?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation describes manual execution and a bypass variable, so teams should restrict bypass use.

faq.question: Is this useful with Codex or Claude?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but the documented native hook integration is for Claude Code.
